description: What each security product is known to emit for AI/LLM analysis. Detect the vendor once, and the pack supplies its taxonomy without enumerating the tenant. Every value here was observed on a live tenant -- add to it after each engagement so customer N+1 starts where customer N finished.

Zscaler/Zscaler Internet Access.notes: Category strings are title-case and differ from Palo Alto's hyphenated taxonomy. 'MS Copilot Personal' distinguishes personal Copilot from the enterprise tenant -- nothing else surfaces that.

Palo Alto Networks/Palo Alto NGFW.notes: Hyphenated lowercase taxonomy in `categories`. AI-platform-service means API/agent traffic rather than chat UI -- a useful shadow-AI signal. Grayware:/Parked: alert prefixes are domain verdicts, not AI alerts.

Check Point/Check Point NGFW.notes: Uses Accept/Prevent, NOT Allow/Block -- a panel filtering on 'Block' matches nothing here. Categories are sparse; most AI traffic carries a null category and is only identifiable by domain.

Check Point/SmartDefense.notes: Emits machine-generated DGA detection tokens (dga-Cai8Z.TC.893fEDbW). Each is unique and never recurs -- 973 distinct values in 30 days on one tenant. Never usable as context-table entries.

Cisco/Cisco Umbrella.notes: DNS-only, and the most commonly mis-analysed source. Events arrive as activity_type dns-response, NOT web-activity-allowed, so the OOTB AI/LLM analytics rules never fire on an Umbrella-only tenant regardless of table health. Domains land in dns_domain (registered domain, e.g. claude.ai) and dns_query (full FQDN) -- never web_domain, so a Web Domains table cannot match. Categories are compound strings; match with RGXi('Generative AI') rather than equality. `user` is blank on ~99.9% of rows, so identity needs Parser Manager mapping or an Entra ID context-table lookup.
observed_on: documented in CLAUDE.md, not yet measured by this module

Exabeam/Observra.notes: Exabeam's agent-level sensor. NAMING: the rename ran ABA -> Observra and finalised 24 June 2026; production Vendor/Product is Exabeam/Observra and the parser requires "schema":"observra. The `aba-` variant is a SUPERSEDED interim name that survives only in the public Content-Library-CIM2 mirror, which froze 16 June -- eight days before the rename -- and publishes it with no freshness marker. Never cite CIM2 for parser definitions; use Parser Manager in the tenant. Verified from Parser_Update-2026-08-06_Observra_2026_07_16. This is the only source of the agent-only fields that block AI rules on proxy/DLP-only tenants, and the only thing that populates `result`, which five of six panels on the OOTB Agentic AI Security dashboard depend on. Parser conditions are literal substrings ANDed and evaluated BEFORE extraction -- miss one and the event lands parsed:false, msg_type:null, no fields, while ingest still returns HTTP 200. `cost_usd` must be top-level; nesting it under data silently drops it. Group detections on ai_agent_name, never agent_name -- the parser maps $.framework to agent_name, so agent_name holds the framework (claude/adk/openai) by design. Ingest is the Webhook Cloud Collector on api2.<region> (EXA-INGEST-API2-HOST). The parser extracts 23 paths, all operational, and drops every security-relevant field (has_injection, current_depth/max_depth, source_agent/target_agent, skill provenance, triggered_rules/max_severity) -- so the behavioural layer works but the deterministic layer cannot be built.

alert_name_templates: Default DLP policy - Protect sensitive M365 Copilot interactions
DSPM for AI: Detect sensitive info added to AI sites
DLP-Audit sensitive data shared to generative AI sites
CC_DSPM for AI - Unethical behavior in AI apps
Microsoft/Microsoft Purview.notes: Two shapes. DSPM-for-AI policies emit a clean policy name straight into alert_name and are table-friendly. Classic DLP policy matches wrap the policy name with the EMAIL SUBJECT -- one distinct value per email, so no exact-match context table can ever match them, and the subjects carry patient/customer content. Apply alert_name_pattern to recover the policy name before diffing; 3,323 distinct values collapsed to 2 policies on one tenant. A tenant emitting no DSPM names has not enabled DSPM for AI -- that is a customer finding, not a tooling gap.

Microsoft/Microsoft 365.notes: Audit operations, not alerts. AIEnterpriseInteractionsExported does not match a \bAI\b word-boundary pattern -- there is no boundary between AI and Enterprise. Any AI classifier must allow a leading AI followed by a capital.

Microsoft/Copilot.notes: M365 Copilot audit is the usual source of ai_agent-* activity. It does NOT populate `result` or `result_reason`, which the OOTB Agentic AI Security dashboard is built on -- five of its six panels hang off `result` (EXA-AGENTIC-DASH-NULL-RESULT). `user` is ~99.8% null; identity is in email_address.

Asimily/Asimily.notes: Medical-device security platform. Emits a genuine, low-cardinality AI alert name -- valuable in healthcare tenants and easily missed because the vendor is not a traditional security feed.

Netskope/Netskope Security Cloud.notes: Present on a healthcare tenant with 14 distinct alert names, none AI-relevant in 30 days. CASB is a likely AI-visibility source; worth probing its own category taxonomy when a tenant relies on it.

Varonis/Varonis Data Security Platform.notes: 27 distinct alert names observed, none AI-relevant in 30 days.

SentinelOne/Singularity Platform.notes: Endpoint source -- the likely provider of process_name / parent_process_name, which are the only detection path for locally-run models (ollama, lm studio, llama.cpp, MCP servers).

SentinelOne/Prompt Security.notes: Dedicated GenAI security platform (acquired by SentinelOne), arriving via a Webhook cloud collector and emitting ai_agent-request. This is an AI-NATIVE source: unlike a proxy it sees prompts and responses rather than domains, so it is a candidate provider of the agent-only fields that block rules on proxy-only tenants. Probe llm_request / llm_response / ai_token_* on any tenant running it before concluding an agent sensor is missing. Do NOT let it inherit the SentinelOne EDR pack -- different product, different role.

CrowdStrike/Falcon.notes: Endpoint process telemetry is the ONLY detection path for locally-run models -- ollama, lm studio, llama.cpp, gpt4all, MCP servers -- which leave no network trace after download and are invisible to every proxy. Feeds the AI Agent Process Names and AI Dev Framework Process Names tables (6 rules each). A tenant with Falcon but empty process-name tables has the telemetry and is simply not matching it.
observed_on: reported present at geha.use1; product string not yet confirmed

Fortinet/FortiGate.notes: FortiGuard web filtering. Category strings UNVERIFIED against a live tenant -- confirm before relying on them.

Okta/Okta.notes: SSO into AI SaaS. The `app` field carries the target application name, which feeds AI/LLM Applications -- often the only record that a sanctioned AI tool is in use when the proxy cannot see inside TLS. Worth probing on any tenant where Applications overlap is low.

Microsoft/Entra ID.notes: Enterprise-app sign-ins name the AI SaaS being accessed, and Entra is also the join that maps a proxy's short directory ID to a person -- the identity gap seen on every proxy-only tenant.

Exabeam/Correlation Rule.notes: Exabeam's own output. Exclude from source inventories -- it is not a customer telemetry source.

Exabeam/Audit Log.notes: Exabeam platform audit. Exclude from source inventories.
